claims_boundary: Partner candidates are screening targets only; no interest, availability, commitment, eligibility, nontraditional status, or teaming agreement is claimed.
DARPA challenge results establish bounded public performance evidence, not suitability for a specific future proposal.
Potential competitive and IP conflicts must be assessed before technical disclosure.
Scores below are internal screening scores, not probabilities of partnership or award.

candidates.name: DefendTex
candidates.public_evidence: DARPA recorded a 12-lb aircraft lifting a 112-lb payload for a 9.63:1 attempted ratio, the highest ratio attempted in the 2026 challenge, but the aircraft did not complete a scored run. DARPA awarded Most Promising Technology and described string-based support to individual motors that reduced hub structure and disk loading.
candidates.best_worldshepherd_role: High-ratio structural/aerodynamic architecture partner; Worldshepherd contributes failure analysis, telemetry provenance, safety-state capture, deterministic mission replay, and completion/reliability test design.
candidates.principal_gap_or_risk: The public evidence is an incomplete run; repeatability, control margins, failure mode, endurance, and 2028 220-lb/10-nm scalability require validation. High direct competitive/IP overlap is possible.

candidates.name: AVIDrone, Inc.
candidates.public_evidence: DARPA's official best completed 2026 scored run was 3.84:1 using a 29-lb aircraft and 112-lb payload. AVIDrone publicly describes heavy-lift aircraft, automated flight, proprietary autopilot, long-range cruise, cargo delivery, and BVLOS-oriented autonomy.
candidates.best_worldshepherd_role: Completed-flight baseline and integrated airframe/autonomy partner; Worldshepherd contributes governed autonomy assurance, mission evidence, APNT/degraded-state test orchestration, and 2028 scaling analysis.
candidates.principal_gap_or_risk: Current official ratio is below 4:1 and far below the Worldshepherd 10:1 research target; proprietary autopilot and direct market overlap may reduce complementarity.

candidates.name: University of Maryland Autonomous Micro Air Vehicle Team / UAS Research and Operations Center
candidates.public_evidence: DARPA awarded UMD Most Revolutionary Aerodynamic Design for a tri-rotor/propeller-driven-rotor aircraft using servo-controlled blade and motor angles to take off as a multirotor and transition after takeoff. UMD reports the team also uses UROC personnel and facilities for UAS design and testing.
candidates.best_worldshepherd_role: Aerodynamics, transition-flight, controls, and independent academic validation partner; Worldshepherd contributes evidence governance, simulation-to-flight discrepancy tracking, and falsification-oriented test campaigns.
candidates.principal_gap_or_risk: Subjective innovation award does not itself establish a high completed payload ratio. University contracting, IP, publication, and schedule terms require screening.

candidates.name: Portal Aircraft Company
candidates.public_evidence: DARPA awarded Portal Most Revolutionary Powertrain Design for a scalable concept using hot or cold turbine exhaust to drive rotors while replacing driveshafts and mechanical linkages, with potential reliability benefit from fewer mechanical components.
candidates.best_worldshepherd_role: Track-B-style powertrain architecture partner; Worldshepherd contributes instrumentation, provenance, mass/thermal/efficiency accounting, lifecycle test orchestration, and system-level assurance.
candidates.principal_gap_or_risk: The public award establishes design novelty, not the >=4:1 DP2 empirical proof required for a prime. Thermal efficiency, exhaust distribution, controls, manufacturability, and IP require validation.

candidates.name: MTech Operations, LLC
candidates.public_evidence: DARPA recorded the second-best completed 2026 scored run at 3.64:1 using a 32-lb aircraft and 117-lb payload.
candidates.best_worldshepherd_role: Completed-flight systems baseline partner for reliability, repeatability, mission replay, and incremental 4:1-to-higher scaling studies.
candidates.principal_gap_or_risk: Public evidence is below 4:1 and limited detail is available on architecture and commercial readiness; additional company and IP diligence is required.

candidates.name: Xtreme Aerial Concepts
candidates.public_evidence: DARPA recorded the third-best completed 2026 scored run at 3.45:1 and awarded third place in the objective performance category.
candidates.best_worldshepherd_role: Independent completed-flight comparison article for benchmarking mass efficiency, test repeatability, and mission-assurance methods.
candidates.principal_gap_or_risk: Public technical detail and integration fit are limited; ratio remains below 4:1. Partner value cannot be inferred from competition placement alone.

recommended_sequence: Perform public IP/prior-art and company-status diligence on DefendTex, AVIDrone, UMD/UROC, Portal, MTech, and Xtreme before outreach.
For 2028 research, prioritize complementary evidence: DefendTex high-ratio structure + UMD transition aerodynamics + Portal powertrain + one completed-run system baseline.

For the September 2026 DP2 topic, do not represent Worldshepherd as prime without its own qualifying empirical evidence; identify whether any candidate already has the topic-specific >=4:1 proof and is seeking assurance/autonomy/integration support.
Use a non-confidential one-page interface/evidence contribution description before any proprietary Worldshepherd disclosure.
